Revert "diagnostics: move mojo_utils to the common directory." This reverts commit 08a7a4e9efb15a848f4fcff8c3ddabb34952f27b. Reason for revert: At the time this commit was landed, we expected cros_healthd to use a similar D-Bus service to wilco_dtc_supportd, and testing that service meant cros_healthd would benefit from having access to mojo_utils. crash-reporter: c++iza anomaly detector and have it use the journal Have anomaly_detector use the systemd journal as its log source instead of reading from /var/log/messages. Audit messages have been moved to /var/log/audit/audit.log, and attempts to make anomaly_detector read two files proved complicated: https://crrev.com/c/1630336 It was cleaner to completely rewrite anomaly detector by migrating it to C++ than to try to fit the current unit tests with the journal implementation. This has the added advantage of reducing the dependencies of the unit test and making it much faster since we no longer need to repeatedly call sleep. It's also now understood by the unit test framework as a group of multiple tests instead of one big test. Reading from journal has several advantages, most of which we aren't taking advantage of in this change, but can done in the future. Possible future improvements: * Use sd_journal_add_match and friends to make following the journal more efficient. * Save the journal cursor between boots to avoid missing certain early-boot and shutdown crashes: https://crbug.com/343954#c8 * Leverage structured audit data. Journald actually has all the audit fields we parse from the audit line as structured data. Use these instead of parsing the audit line. BUG=chromium:894029,chromium:874698,chromium:326840 TEST=unit tests Cq-Depend: chromium:1670435 Change-Id: I17613ca70e0c7c97c253aba6be57fa33aba7bc33 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1680651 Tested-by: Chris Morin <cmtm@chromium.org> Commit-Ready: Miriam Zimmerman <mutexlox@chromium.org> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Mike Frysinger <vapier@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Jeffrey Kardatzke <jkardatzke@google.com>

dlcservice: Unify into simple logic for exposed APIs Dlcservice exposes 3 main APIs: - Install - Uninstall - GetInstall Within this CL, we try and break those APIs into calling helpers for high level understanding that is simple. Sequence of events that should happen for each API: - Install: CreateDlc - Uninstall: UnmountDlc, DeleteDlc - GetInstall: Just return the installed DLC(s). Currently these APIs are dependent on the fact that |LoadDlcModuleImages()| will always fully succeed and give rise to a |installed_dlc_modules_| that is completely valid. |OnStatusUpdateAdvancedSignal()| will only return a single type of error as the user should not care whether |ImageLoader| was the reason for the failure, but the mounting itself failed. This will require improvements to |MountDlc()|. Note: No breakage of old unittests. BUG=none TEST=FEATURES="test" emerge-$BOARD dlcservice TEST=tast run $TEST_IP platform.DLCService Change-Id: I62e2e1b4df8b310fc08eb215e0874f94e21ed2fa Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1730169 Tested-by: Jae Hoon Kim <kimjae@chromium.org> Commit-Ready: Jae Hoon Kim <kimjae@chromium.org> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Xiaochu Liu <xiaochu@chromium.org>

shill: connection: Add oif rules for all interfaces Previously, a pair of iif rules were added for all physical interfaces. However, this still left an edge case in which a socket has SO_BINDTODEVICE but does not have bind() explicitly called. In this case, at connect() time, the socket is still implicitly bound to INADDR_ANY (for AF_INET sockets), and source address selection must occur. However, lacking any oif rules, our set of policy rules has nothing to distinguish this source address selection case from regular source address selection. Therefore when the socket is bound to a device that is not the primary interface on the system, the bound device and the outcome of source address selection are in disagreement. This change adds a pair of oif rules for all interfaces so that source address selection takes any potential bound device into account. Adding this functionality required providing support for FRA_OIFNAME in shill. Note that all of our kernel trees define this routing policy type. cryptohome: Add new commandline features for cryptohome commandline tool. To add new data restore key, simply type: cryptohome --action=add_data_restore_key --user=your_user_name Then type in your password, wait for a few second, then the hex string of data restore key will be displayed if authenticated. To build authentication, testers can use switch "--restore_key_in_hex" to provide data restore key in HexString, for instance if testers type: cryptohome --action=check_key_ex --user=your_user_name --restore_key_in_hex=0123456789ABCDEF Cryptohome will use restore key in AuthorizationRequest and check if it can be authenticated. To mass remove keys, users need to provide exempt key labels. Every other keyset whose label is not in exempt_key_labels will be removed. For instance, if users have four keysets which are labeled as "l1", "l2", "l3" and "l4", say if they want to delete l1 and l2 and keep l3 and l4, they should type: cryptohome --action=mass_remove_keys --user=your_user_name --exempt_key_labels=l3,l4 After authenticated, l1 and l2 will be removed. BUG=chromium:945057 TEST=Flash image to physical device and use cryptohome command line to test.
